answers.answer: Yes, there is an EI caregiving benefit for a critically ill child under 18. [1]

Support is defined as providing psychological or emotional support to a critically ill or injured person or someone needing end-of-life care. A critically ill or injured person is someone whose baseline state of health has changed significantly because of illness or injury. As a result, their life is at risk as a direct or indirect result of illness or injury and care or support is needed from at least 1 caregiver. Their condition must be certified by a medical doctor or nurse practitioner. If the person is already living with a chronic medical condition, caregivers aren't eligible for benefits unless the person’s health changes significantly because of a new and acute life-threatening event.

answers.q: Who can get the Guaranteed Income Supplement?
answers.answer: The Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) is available to individuals who are 65 years of age or older. [1]

sources.text: The Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) is a monthly, tax-free payment you can get if you are 65 or older. In most cases, Service Canada will be able to automatically enroll you for the supplement if we have your eligibility information. Service Canada will inform you by mail. If it's been one month since your 64th birthday and you still have not received an enrollment letter, you may need to apply.

You can also report your income directly to us to renew or confirm your eligibility. If you have questions or concerns about your GIS payments, contact us . The Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) is a monthly, tax-free payment you can get if you are 65 or older.

If you haven't filed your 2025 taxes with the CRA, your Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) payments may stop or be reduced. To avoid interruptions, file your taxes as soon as possible. You can also report your income directly to us to renew or confirm your eligibility.

answers.q: Qu'est-ce que l'allocation canadienne pour enfants et quels enfants vise-t-elle?
answers.answer:
L'allocation canadienne pour enfants (ACE) est un montant mensuel non imposable versé aux familles admissibles pour aider à subvenir aux besoins de leurs enfants de moins de 18 ans. Ce montant peut inclure des montants spécifiques pour les enfants handicapés et des programmes provinciaux ou territoriaux connexes. Il est administré par l'Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC).

answers.q: What happened to the GST/HST credit in July 2026?
answers.answer: In July 2026, the GST/HST credit was replaced by the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB). [2]

sources.text: Additional one-time top-up payment issued June 5, 2026 The additional one-time GST/HST credit top-up payment was issued on June 5, 2026 to provide immediate support before the CGEB took effect in July 2026. If you were entitled to receive the GST/HST credit in January 2026, you would have received this one-time payment. For details: One-time GST/HST credit top-up payment

Replaced with: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) The GST/HST credit has been renamed the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) as of July 2026. The GST/HST credit was a tax-free quarterly payment for individuals and families with low and modest incomes to help offset the GST or HST they paid. Payments may have included amounts from provincial or territorial programs which will now be included with your CGEB payments.

Since the credit has been renamed the CGEB, any retroactive payment amount you are entitled to will be issued as a CGEB payment. Depending on when your previous year return is assessed, you may receive your retroactive amount as a separate lump sum payment or combined with your next quarterly CGEB payment. The GST/HST credit was recalculated every July based on the information from the previous year’s tax return. Payment periods started in July and ended in June of the following year. Last quarterly payment under the GST/HST credit was issued April 2, 2026 .

sources.text: The Canada Disability Benefit (CDB) provides direct financial support to people with disabilities who are between 18 and 64 years old.
